title: The Ghost Blimp That Landed With No Pilots

basis.note: not enough measured videos yet; using fixed default

segments.narration: August 16, 1942. A Navy blimp drifted out of the Pacific fog and scraped along a quiet street in Daly City.
First responders pried open the gondola door. Inside: a working radio, a wet raincoat, and the throttle still set to half-power.
Two veteran pilots were gone. So ask yourself: how do two men evaporate in mid-air without ever touching the radio?
Navy ships searched miles of open ocean. No parachutes were deployed. No bodies ever washed ashore.
The blimp's flight recorder proved the aircraft never touched the water. Whatever took those pilots came from inside the sky.

verdicts.claim: On August 16, 1942, US Navy blimp L-8 landed on a street in Daly City, California.
verdicts.note: The reference article confirms that L-8 crashed in the street in front of a house on Bellevue Avenue in Daly City on August 16, 1942.

verdicts.claim: The two crew members, Lieutenant Ernest Dewitt Cody and Ensign Charles Ellis Adams, were missing.
verdicts.note: The reference article confirms Lieutenant Ernest DeWitt Cody and Ensign Charles Adams were missing and no traces of them were ever found.

verdicts.claim: The blimp's radio was operational and the throttle was set to half-power upon landing.
verdicts.note: The reference article mentions that the radio and engines were switched on, but it does not mention the throttle setting.

verdicts.claim: No parachutes were used and no bodies were ever found.
verdicts.note: The article confirms all three parachutes were left behind in the gondola and no traces or bodies of the missing crew were ever found.
